quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your ability to ride?

options.text: At about half the legal limit

questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your motorcycle. It contains specifications, operating instructions, and maintenance suggestions for your specific bike.

questions.question: What rule applies when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit to complete the pass
You can ignore no-passing zones if you started in a passing zone
You can pass on the shoulder
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal zones

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal zones
questions.explanation: Always pass within posted speed limits and only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit for best protection?

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely
Be loose and flap in the wind
Only partially cover your arms and legs

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely
questions.explanation: Good protection requires jackets and pants that cover all of your arms and legs. They should fit snugly but allow free movement. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Is a helmet required when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Only if you have had your license for two years or less

questions.explanation: In Vermont, all motorcycle riders and passengers must wear a helmet. A DOT-approved helmet is the most effective protection against serious injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see clearly to the sides for safe riding
It does not have a chin strap

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see clearly to the sides for safe riding
questions.explanation: Helmets do not limit your side vision. Any DOT-approved helmet allows the wearer to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a vehicle's blind spot?

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver
Wave to get the driver's attention
Slow down and move out of the blind spot

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and move out of the blind spot
questions.explanation: If you are in a blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to get out of it.

questions.question: What should you check about your brakes before riding?

options.text: They make a loud squeaking noise
They cause friction with the steering
Each brake can hold the motorcycle
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Each one should feel firm and hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: How should you position your motorcycle when stopped behind another vehicle?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle
Do not use your mirrors to watch traffic behind you
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if a vehicle approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials, especially at night. Bright colors and reflective materials help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, you should look at all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What is the main active substance in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active substance in marijuana is THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make hand gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass if you can. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and increase danger.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, oil, and metal plates are slippery. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors when riding to help others see you, even in daylight.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Does not affect how a motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for new riders.
Can change how a motorcycle handles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how a motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to a motorcycle and changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control a motorcycle.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. Take a rest break at least every two hours on long trips. This helps prevent fatigue.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: When you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that lets you draft off other vehicles.
The one where other drivers can see you.
The one in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one where other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen by them. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears. Choose a position that gives you the most space around you.

questions.question: What should you check before you ride?

options.text: How much padding your seat has

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle. Look at your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
